assessment.nobel_worthiness: The framework transformed modern empirical and quantitative trade analysis by making firm selection and heterogeneity central to the gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the central originator, with Helpman and Redding making major complementary theoretical and quantitative contributions.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are deeply embedded in trade research and have generated an extensive empirical literature.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of credit among foundational contributors remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural methods for demand, competition, and industry dynamics supplied a durable empirical framework for evaluating market power and policy.
assessment.attribution: Pakes, Berry, and Bresnahan are especially closely associated with key foundational advances, though the listed field has many important contributors.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been tested and extended across industries for decades and is central to modern industrial organization.
uncertainties: A three-person award cannot fully represent the broad set of methodological contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of work provided core economic tools for understanding network effects, standards, platform competition, and digital-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Shapiro, Varian, and Farrell made highly visible foundational contributions, while Katz and Athey also represent substantial relevant work.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical insights have long informed research, antitrust analysis, and the interpretation of digital markets.
uncertainties: The breadth of the digital-economics label makes the exact boundary of the contribution difficult to define.
Credit allocation among closely related contributors is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis and measurement of reciprocity, fairness, and inequity aversion changed economic models of behavior in markets and organizations.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt are particularly associated with formal inequity-aversion models, and Falk made major related experimental contributions.
assessment.maturity: The concepts have been replicated, applied widely, and incorporated into broad areas of economic research.
uncertainties: Experimental findings and their interpretation can vary with institutional setting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established management practices and organizational capital as measurable, economically consequential sources of productivity differences.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are the leading architects of the research program; Sadun made important extensions and applications.
assessment.maturity: A substantial international evidence base now connects management measurement to firm performance and policy-relevant questions.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation and the portability of measured practices across settings remain active empirical questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design created a powerful general framework for strategic communication and information policy.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow introduced the canonical persuasion framework, while Bergemann supplied major foundational contributions to information design.
assessment.maturity: The framework has rapidly become a standard tool with applications in economics and related fields.
uncertainties: Its comparatively recent expansion leaves less time to judge its ultimate empirical and policy influence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work gave trade policy a rigorous political-economy foundation and clarified how organized interests shape protection.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are directly and distinctly identified with the central theoretical program.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is longstanding, influential, and remains a benchmark for research on trade and politics.
uncertainties: Empirical applications may depend strongly on institutional and political context.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made forward-looking structural models operational for major applied economic questions.
assessment.attribution: Rust is the clearest foundational figure, with Keane and Eckstein contributing major developments and applications.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been used and refined extensively over several decades across labor, industrial organization, and other fields.
uncertainties: Structural results can be sensitive to modeling assumptions and computational choices.
